title: Account Partition Active
prompt: A TypeScript admin page splits accounts into active and inactive groups. Write a function that returns { active, inactive } arrays in original order.

explanation.beginner:
Example: accountPartitionActive([{"id":"1","active":true},{"id":"2","active":false}]) produces {"active":[{"id":"1","active":true}],"inactive":[{"id":"2","active":false}]}. Create separate result buckets and route each input to exactly one according to its predicate.

Compare “handles empty arrays”: input [[]] produces {"active":[],"inactive":[]}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Create separate result buckets and route each input to exactly one according to its predicate.

Tempting mistake: Two unrelated filters can drift apart and accidentally drop or duplicate records. Check that the partition preserves the input count.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles empty arrays”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
